debt_events.summary: Completed exchange of 97.44% of previously outstanding 2027 convertible notes for $209.721 million principal of 7% convertible senior secured second-lien PIK-toggle notes due 2030 (including the $12.5 million premium) and 317,834,446 common shares. Company classified the transaction as a troubled debt restructuring under ASC 470-60; this is not an agency default rating.

Latest filed 10-Q reports first-lien delayed-draw term-loan facility of $100 million, maturing February 7, 2030, with 12% interest compounded quarterly and paid in kind. Company reported compliance with both loan-agreement and 2030-note covenants at June 27, 2026; this does not establish compliance at November 9.

Second supplemental indenture removed certain restrictions on repurchasing or exchanging remaining 2027 notes for cash and/or equity; extended the 2030 notes make-whole period from October 15, 2028 to January 15, 2029.

Exchanged $15 million principal of 2027 notes for approximately 1.55 million common shares. As of September 26, 2026, $14.5 million principal remained outstanding, due March 15, 2027; the exchange preserves cash but further dilutes equity.

output.risk_rationale: As of November 9, 2026, high credit and counterparty risk reflects continued losses and cash consumption, the October 2025 troubled debt restructuring and subsequent debt-for-equity exchanges, plus a delayed Q3 filing. The September 26 cash balance excluding restricted cash of $154.623 million, against $85.625 million current liabilities and only $14.5 million remaining March 2027 notes, provides a meaningful near-term buffer, but $313.9 million reported debt carrying value and negative $24.556 million quarterly adjusted EBITDA leave repayment dependent on turnaround execution. Historical supplier-payment delays and the $15.438 million trademark judgment strengthen the case for tight counterparty limits and short settlement terms; no current agency rating or verified payment default was established.

distress_signals.summary: Filed notification that the September 26, 2026 Form 10-Q would be late because financial-close procedures and documentation for asset impairment and lease modifications were incomplete. Expected filing by November 10, 2026, without assurance; therefore the latest opened filed quarterly report is Q2, while the newer Q3 financials above come from the November 4 unaudited earnings release.

Q3 revenue fell 8.1% year over year; adjusted EBITDA remained negative $24.6 million. Operating loss included $57.1 million of non-cash long-lived-asset impairments and $20.8 million of accelerated rent expense from a further partial headquarters lease termination. U.S. retail distribution losses and lower international foodservice volumes also weighed on sales.

FY2025 annual report describes workforce reductions approved February 24 (approximately 44 North America/EU employees plus approximately 20 China employees) and August 6 (approximately 40 North America employees). China operational activities ceased by year-end 2025; annual report filed April 9, 2026.

Terminated corporate controller and principal accounting officer Yi (Jevy) Luo, effective December 23. CFO and treasurer Lubi Kutua assumed principal-accounting-officer responsibilities pending a replacement; this was not a disclosed CFO departure.

Latest filed quarterly report says the company no longer met Form S-3 eligibility requirements and could not access its at-the-market equity program. Management nevertheless expected existing cash and anticipated operating cash flows to fund foreseeable requirements for the next twelve months, subject to revenue, cash-flow and working-capital assumptions.

payment_behaviour.summary: Food Dive, citing Creditsafe data for July 2025, reported days beyond payment terms of 19, versus 8 in August 2024 and an industry average of 12. About half of outstanding bills were 1–30 days overdue. Beyond Meat pointed to the data provider’s accuracy/completeness disclaimer; this is historical third-party evidence, not verified current arrears.

Court entered a $15,437,500 judgment in the Sonate/Vegadelphia trademark case: $37,500 actual damages plus $15.4 million disgorgement, reduced from the earlier $38.9 million jury award. Further motions or appeals remained possible; this is a litigation obligation, not evidence of a supplier-payment default or an unpaid judgment. Disclosed September 22, 2026.
